style.a: Idempotency means that sending the same request many times produces the same final state as sending it once, so retries do not create duplicate records. It is a property of the operation, not of the HTTP method: GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent by design, while POST is not. Idempotency protects against transient failures and retries, but it does not make a request atomic or safe against concurrent updates.

I don't have access to your hardware or sensors — a laptop's CPU temperature is a live measurement that changes with load, cooling, and ambient temperature, and it's not stored in the model. A secret committed to a repository can be exposed in version history, pull requests, CI logs, and any clone or mirror, and removing it from the working tree does not erase those historical records. Secrets must therefore be excluded from the repository and injected at runtime through environment variables or a secrets manager.

Python threads share the interpreter and GIL, so CPU-bound work cannot use more than one core at a time. Multiprocessing spawns separate processes, each with its own interpreter and memory, and can therefore use multiple cores. The trade-off is interprocess communication and serialization, so multiprocessing is not automatically faster for every workload.
`netstat -tlnp | grep 8080` shows listening sockets and the owning PID; on Linux you can also use `ss -tlnp | grep 8080`. The process name comes from `/proc/<PID>/comm`.

Un load balancer distribuisce le richieste tra più istanze, evitando che una sola sia sovraccarica. Usa algoritmi diversi: round-robin gira le richieste in sequenza, least-connections manda a chi ha meno connessioni aperte, e least-response-time a chi risponde più in fretta. Il vantaggio è scalabilità e resilienza: se un nodo cade, il load balancer smette di inviarci traffico. Il limite è che il nodo che riceve la richiesta non vede il resto del cluster, quindi il load balancer deve conoscere lo stato delle istanze.
